title: Partition Function Form Games: Coalitional Games with Externalities
abstract: A monograph on cooperative games with externalities — partition function form games. The book develops solution concepts for coalition-formation settings where the value of a coalition depends on the structure of competing coalitions. It synthesises the author's research on the recursive core, coalition-structure core, and externalities in cooperative game theory, with applications to international environmental agreements, institutional design, and voting power.
summary_en: Kóczy's monograph develops the theory of partition-function-form games — cooperative games where coalition payoffs depend on the embedding partition of all players, not just the coalition itself. The book covers the foundational solution concepts (recursive core, optimistic/pessimistic variants), comparison with normal-form approaches, applications to international agreements and oligopoly, and connects to the broader cooperative-game-theory literature. It serves as the canonical reference for researchers and graduate students working with games with externalities.
data_used: Theoretical monograph. References numerous applied examples from international relations, industrial organisation, and mechanism design.
policy_relevance: Reference work for researchers at Hungarian institutions (KRTK Game Theory group, BME, Corvinus) working on cooperative-game applications to EU policy, energy markets, climate negotiations, and intergovernmental bargaining. The framework underpins multiple Hungarian policy-relevant papers on EU voting power and energy-coalition analysis.
